newsitem.title: DUBAI: Yemen plans new crude unit at Aden refinery site.
newsitem.headline: Yemen plans new crude unit at Aden refinery site.

text.p: Yemen is studying a fresh proposal to build a new crude distillation unit (CDU) at its Aden oil refinery site, Yemen oil sources said on Tuesday.

Britain's Wimpey, part of construction group Tarmac Plc, has submitted a plan for a single 80,000-120,000 barrels per day (bpd) capacity CDU alongside the existing 42-year-old Aden refinery site, the sources in Aden said.

Earlier proposals for the refinery's future centred on expanding and upgrading the plant to allow it to operate at 170,000 bpd with two CDUs, but this has apparently been dropped because of the high cost.
"A 150,000-170,000 bpd plant is out of the question for the time being," a Yemeni oil official said.
Yemen is the Arab world's poorest country with a relatively low oil production of around 350,000 bpd, and Aden is its only refinery.

Though the Aden hydroskimming plant has a design capacity of 170,000 bpd, actual runs are limited to around 100,000 bpd because of the age and configuration of the refinery which was also damaged during the country's 1994 civil war.

Wimpey and ABB Lummus Global, part of engineering group Asea Brown Boveri Ltd, secured a letter of intent from Yemen's Ministry of Petroleum and Mineral Resources last month to carry out major improvements at the plant.
No final decision had yet been made on whether the refinery's existing CDU will be replaced or remain in operation with a new CDU, the official said.
A decision on the size and configuration of the Aden site well as how financing for the $200-million-plus project will be raised is expected to be made at the end of 1996.
